title: Smooth affine frontier refinement with finite-subfield models
statement:
Fix a prime power $q$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism; def-weil-finite-type-morphism], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change], and let $(T_\nu)$ be a finite partition of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ into locally closed reduced $k$-subschemes [def-constructible-stratification; def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction; def-pc-reduced-scheme]. No Frobenius stability of the $T_\nu$ is assumed.

There is $m\geq1$, with $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$ and $X_m=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$, and a finite chain of reduced closed $k_m$-subschemes
$$Z_0=(X_m)_{\mathrm{red}}\supset Z_1\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing,$$
such that every $U_a=Z_a\setminus Z_{a+1}$ is a finite disjoint union $\coprod_{b\in B_a}U_{a,b}$ of nonempty smooth geometrically connected affine $k_m$-schemes, each smooth of one constant relative dimension $d_{a,b}\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms; def-pc-geometrically-irreducible; def-pc-scheme]. The pieces are open and closed in $U_a$, and the geometric base change of each $U_{a,b}$ is contained as a locally closed subscheme in some $T_\nu$. If $d_{a,b}=0$, then $U_{a,b}\cong\operatorname{Spec}k_m$. Closed and open inclusions have the meanings of [def-weil-closed-immersion; def-weil-open-immersion]. Every chain inclusion, component inclusion and displayed isomorphism is defined over this same $k_m$. For $X_0=\varnothing$ the chain has length zero.

proof.text: If $X_0=\varnothing$, take $m=1$ and the empty chain. Otherwise $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ is finite type over the field $k$, hence Noetherian; reduction has the same underlying topological space. We work with the reduced induced closed subscheme $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and the given finite locally closed partition (intersecting each $T_\nu$ with the reduction). The field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 0B8X; the finite-type and reduction conventions used in the proof

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian good-refinement lemma to the finite partition of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its finite locally closed refinement has the frontier property: the closure of every refined part is a union of refined parts. In particular each refined part lies in one of the original $T_\nu$, and the closure filtration can be ordered so that removing a union of maximal parts leaves a closed subset.

We now construct the pieces by strong induction on closed subsets. For a nonempty reduced closed subscheme $Y$ of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$, take its finitely many irreducible components. For each component $C$, the locally closed part of the refined partition containing its generic point contains a nonempty open of $C$: remove the other components and use the locally closed description. Intersect this open with the dense smooth locus supplied by [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open] (geometric reducedness follows from [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect]) and then with an affine principal open. The resulting $U_C$ is nonempty, smooth, affine, irreducible, and lies in the selected original $T_\nu$. The $U_C$ are pairwise disjoint after removing the other components.

source.place: Tag 0B8X, lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field; affine shrinking in the proof

proof.text: The finite union $U=\coprod_CU_C$ is open in $Y$ and dense in every component. Its complement is a proper closed subset of $Y$; equip it with the reduced induced structure and apply the induction hypothesis. The resulting closed complements give a finite chain $Y=Y_0\supset Y_1\supset\cdots\supset Y_r=\varnothing$, and each difference is the finite disjoint union of the selected $U_C$ belonging to that stage. The frontier property from Step 2 ensures that each difference is open in the corresponding $Y_a$ and that every closure is a union of later differences.

source.place: Tag 0B8X and Tag 06LH; Noetherian induction in the proof paragraphs 6-7

proof.text: Each selected $U_C$ is irreducible, hence connected. Over the algebraically closed field $k$, connectedness after every field extension is geometric connectedness. Smoothness has locally constant fibre dimension by [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant]; since $U_C$ is connected, this dimension is one integer $d_C\ge0$. Thus the geometric chain has exactly the asserted smooth, geometrically connected affine pieces and constant dimensions.

source.place: Tag 0B8X; Tag 02G1 for local constancy of relative dimension

proof.text: There are only finitely many schemes, inclusions, affine charts, component inclusions, and containment relations in this construction. All are of finite presentation over $k$. Regard $k=\varinjlim_n\mathbf F_{q^n}$ as the directed union of its finite subfields. The finite-presentation spreading-out theorem [thm-pd-spreading-out] descends this entire finite diagram, including the closed chain and all open immersions, to one stage $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}$; enlarge $m$ so that the descended equations for every inclusion into the selected $T_\nu$ hold after geometric base change. The resulting base changes are the original $Z_a$ and $U_{a,b}$, so the displayed containment in some $T_\nu$ is preserved.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, clauses (1)--(3); finite constant-field model construction in blueprint proof paragraphs 6-7

proof.text: At the descended stage, smoothness of every affine piece follows after increasing $m$ from [lem-weil-pbc-descend-smooth-qcqs], applied to the finite-presentation piece morphisms over the system of finite fields. The open immersions persist by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-open-immersion-qcqs], while the chain inclusions $Z_{a+1}\hookrightarrow Z_a$ persist as closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion]. Affineness is retained by choosing the descended affine charts from their finite algebra presentations. Finally apply [lem-zl-affine-geometric-components-finite-extension] to each descended affine smooth model and enlarge $m$ once more; its geometrically connected component whose geometric fibre is $U_{a,b}$ is then defined over $k_m$. All finitely many enlargements are replaced by one common multiple.

source.place: Tag 0C0C and Tag 0EUU; Tag 038E for finite-field component descent

proof.text: The finite-field chain is $Z_0=(X_m)_{\mathrm{red}}\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing$, and its differences are the finite disjoint unions just constructed. Each component piece is open and closed in its difference $U_a$ because the components were separated by the principal-open construction and the frontier ordering. Every object and inclusion is defined over $k_m$. If one piece has dimension zero, Tag 06LH first makes it finite over $k_m$; smoothness makes it reduced, so geometric connectedness leaves a single reduced point, and its residue field must equal $k_m$ because the geometric base change is connected. Thus $U_{a,b}\cong\operatorname{Spec}k_m$. This proves every clause of the statement.
